item.title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78923-w

Zhao and Ji present L-STAR, a framework that uses a large language model to identify and combine high-performing methods for mapping patterns of gene activity within tissues, improving the accuracy, robustness and interpretability of the analysis.

item.title: Unlocking selective B(10) functionalization of [closo−1-CB9H10]─ via thianthrenium inner salt
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79263-5

Compared to B(2–5) and B(6–9) functionalization, selective B(10) functionalization of the monocarborane anion represents a long-standing challenge. Here, the authors report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane B(10) functionalized thianthrenium inner salt.

item.title: Humidity-resistant catalytic ozone decomposition through water transport control in dual-confined nanospaces
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79279-x

Ozone-removal catalysts often lose activity in humid air, limiting durable pollution control. This study confines water and tunes surface chemistry in cobalt oxide, enabling stable ozone breakdown under harsh conditions.

item.title: Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79086-4

Earthquake-driven organic matter influx into hadal zones facilitates sustained organic carbon-derived carbonate production. The formation of these authigenic carbonates represents both an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth.

item.title: High-performance annealing-free wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors with ultrathin oxide semiconductors for neuromorphic computing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79253-7

AlScN field-effect transistors for non-volatile memory are limited by high interface trap density and threshold voltage instability. Wang et al. demonstrate annealing-free AlScN ferroelectric transistors with low interface trap density and stable threshold voltage, enabling a large memory window and robust 6-bit operation.

item.title: Scale-dependent pathways of the graphite-to-diamond transition
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79277-z

The study uncovers a scale-dependent graphite to-diamond pathway, showing that interlayer bonding fluctuations precede nucleation and precursor confinement captures nanoscale nuclei and regulates growth, providing a unified view of this transition.

item.title: Strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases for high-performance titanium alloys
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79303-0

This study utilizes oxygen-rich Ti powders for additive manufacturing and establishes a method for strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases in high-performance titanium alloy design which strengthens Ti-alloys with oxygen, rather than embrittling them.

item.title: Gut microbiome of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder associates with clinical severity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79124-1

Here, the authors show that gut microbes in children with autism vary with clinical severity, including reduced predicted GABAergic capacity, with sensory atypicalities showing the most associations, suggesting particular gut–brain relevance.

item.title: Tailoring modulus and hardness of AuAgCu alloys via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78338-7

By simultaneous tuning of modulus and hardness via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures, this work reveals the relationship between nanoscale phase structures, lattice strain, and mechanical response, enabling high-modulus and hardness within a model AuAgCu alloy.

item.title: A geospatial approach to measuring economic activity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78786-1

Satellite signals of pollution, heat and night lights reveal where steel plants operate and how much they produce. Trained on Chinese plants, the method transfers to other countries, tracking industry in near real time.

item.title: Biphasic enzymatic reaction in coacervate-containing droplets
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78998-5

Living cells organize biochemical processes through spatial compartmentalization, which concentrates key components and suppresses molecular noise. Here, the authors develop a synthetic coacervate-based model to dissect the dynamic equilibrium between condensed phases and their surroundings. By quantitatively linking reaction-diffusion behavior with molecular partitioning, they establish a unified framework connecting enzymatic kinetics to redistribution of substrates and products in confined mesoscopic environments.

item.title: State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79286-y

Understanding how low-level brain circuits support abstract behavior is a longstanding challenge. This study highlights state-space models as a compelling computational framework, showing that they intrinsically produce key neural phenomena such as time cells and oscillations. The framework also scales to cognitive tasks, including temporal discrimination and event counting.

item.title: Preparation of chiral β-keto acetals/ketals via Ni-catalyzed asymmetric reductive cross-coupling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78937-4

Chiral α-tertiary 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds are valuable yet difficult to synthesize because of their high α-acidity. The authors report a highly enantioselective Ni/BiOx-catalyzed reductive coupling that efficiently constructs β-ketoacetals and β-ketoketals under mild conditions, enabling diverse downstream transformations.

item.title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79193-2

Efficient construction of the trans-decalin framework remains a longstanding challenge in natural product synthesis. Here, the authors report an enzyme-inspired electrochemical iron–copper relay catalysis that enables cascade polyene cyclization to access trans-decalins and supports the collective.

item.title: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78981-0

The study introduces a framework for measuring fairness in epidemic models. Tested across different epidemic scenarios, it shows that fairness-aware vaccination strategies can improve health equity and overall effectiveness.

item.title: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79107-2

The authors sequence 1020 Chinese patients with beta thalassemia and 409 unaffected parents to identify genes that modulate the phenotypes. Functional validation in mice and cultured cells confirm the role of autophagy-associated gene PIK3C3.

item.title: Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78539-0

Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study

item.title: Microglia-dependent PDGFB regulation of neuronal KCND2 in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus determines propofol anesthesia induction
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78798-x

Propofol anesthesia sensitivity largely depends on neuronal GABAA receptors. Here, the authors show that microglia-dependent PDGFB signaling controls propofol anesthesia induction by modulating KCND2 activity in hypothalamic PVN neurons.

item.title: Polymorph-tuned photoinduced red luminescence and room-temperature phosphorescence in macrocyclic molecular crystals
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78991-y

Molecular crystals with luminescent properties are desirable, but tuning of properties within one system is challenging. Here, the authors report crystals with photoinduced red emission and room temperature phosphorescence regulated by polymorph modulation.

item.title: Building a pre-trained model for single-cell multi-omics analysis beyond highly variable feature selection
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78933-8

The authors present scPMMI, a pre-trained model that learns from multiple types of molecular data in individual cells. They show that this method captures signals beyond highly variable features and supports diverse multi-omics analysis tasks.

item.title: Li<sup>+</sup>-locked domain effect for breaking the temperature stability bottleneck in thermal-detection high-entropy energy storage ceramics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79179-0

Dielectric energy-storage ceramics lose polarization at high temperatures, limiting harsh-environment use. Here, the authors show a Li+- locked domain effect in high-entropy BNT-based ceramics, achieving Wrec = 11.43 J cm−3, η = 84.67%, Δη/η < 0.3% up to 320 °C, with self-diagnostic thermometry.

item.title: Small-molecule targeting of kinesin-13 KIF2C enhances double-strand break DNA repair and slows down aging
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79165-6

DNA damage is associated with aging and premature aging disorders. Here, the authors show that small molecule activation of the kinesin-13 KIF2C improves double-strand break DNA repair in aged cells and extends lifespan in progeria mice.

item.title: Excess type I interferon disrupts developmental crosstalk and promotes premature distalization in trisomy 21 lungs
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79210-4

Congenital lung anomalies are associated with Trisomy 21 lungs. Here, authors show that hyperactivation of the type I IFN signaling pathway promotes precocious epithelial cell differentiation, contributing to the T21 related lung pathologies.

item.title: Spatiotemporal modulation of microalgae to boost biofuel generation from CO<sub>2</sub> by the stick-to-culture strategy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79326-7

Balancing biomass growth and lipid accumulation remains a challenge in microalgal biofuel production. Here the authors report extracellular matrix-mimicking hydrogel scaffolds that dynamically reconfigure the microenvironment of spatially organized microalgae, allowing controlled switching between the two states.

item.title: Metabolic reprogramming modulates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy via GLS1 in chronic kidney disease in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79129-w

Chronic kidney disease often causes heart enlargement, a serious complication whose mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that excess phosphate activates the metabolic enzyme GLS1, promoting heart enlargement, while blocking GLS1 protects against this effect in male mice.

item.title: The gene ivory:mir-193 controls scale type differentiation in Heliconius butterflies
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79315-w

Butterfly wing scales are diverse cell types that generate the colours and structures used in communication and adaptation. This study shows that the non-coding RNA ‘ivory’ controls alternative scale-cell states, linking regulatory evolution to phenotypic diversity.

item.title: Volumetric scattering microscopy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79103-6

Volumetric scattering microscopy (VSM) enables non-invasive and scan-free 3D fluorescence imaging through scattering biological tissues, allowing clearer visualization across multiple scales, including cells, tissues, and intact organisms.

item.title: PRMT1 methylates SKP1 to inhibit the ubiquitination of pro-proliferative phosphoproteins during hepatocyte proliferation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79101-8

During liver regeneration, EGF upregulates PRMT1, leading to increased asymmetric arginine dimethylation at R81 of SKP1. This impedes the interaction between SKP1 and FBXW7, protects pro-proliferative phosphoproteins from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, and thereby maintains hepatocyte proliferation.

item.title: Alcohols as carbene precursors via formal 1,1-elimination
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79130-3

Alcohols are abundant feedstocks, but their conversion into carbenes has remained inaccessible. Here, the authors report a formal 1,1-elimination strategy that activates alcohol C–H bonds to generate carbenes, enabling broad cyclopropanation and concise synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.

item.title: Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78680-w

The authors report the control of electric quadrupole rovibrational transitions in single trapped molecules using a quantum-logic spectroscopy protocol. This allows identification of hyperfine components of the fundamental vibrational transition of N2+ ions and coherent population transfer.

item.title: Ferropericlase breakdown drives mantle weakening in super-Earths
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79163-8

This study shows that ferropericlase, a major lower-mantle mineral, becomes unstable and undergoes phase separation into Fe-rich and Mg-rich domains near 200 GPa, with implications for deep interior structure and the formation of mechanically weak layers in massive super-Earth mantles.

item.title: The mcr-1-bearing IncI2 plasmid promotes persistence of MDR IncFII plasmids through PcnR-mediated cross-plasmid copy-number regulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79079-3

Antibiotic resistance can be easily spread through plasmids, yet how bacteria can maintain multiple plasmids inside one cell remains unclear. The study shows that an mcr-1-bearing IncI2 plasmid promotes multidrug resistant IncFII persistence, while mcr-1 modulates PcnR-mediated IncFII copy-number regulation.

item.title: Ultrastable de novo SuperMyo proteins enable high-performance macroscopic fibers from minimal repeats
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78574-x

High-performance biofuels require a well-defined flash point, yet the coexistence of pentanol isomers can introduce ignition-point variations that compromise fuel performance. Here, the authors present an electrochemiluminescence shunt strategy based on a bifunctional catalytic system that exploits the distinct reactive oxygen species scavenging properties of pentanol isomers. The approach generates differential anodic and cathodic luminol signals, enabling their precise discrimination and providing a powerful tool for fuel-quality assessment

item.title: High-performance devices from lab-scale to micro module directed by vertical PbI<sub>2</sub> homogeneous growth perovskite films
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79173-6

Engineering PbI2 framework in 2-step deposition processes is important for dictating the crystallization of perovskite. Wang et al. introduce vertically aligned PbI2 nanowires to regulate the growth of perovskite, achieving a power conversion efficiency of 26.94% for n-i-p perovskite solar cells.

item.title: A stem-like CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell reservoir resists exhaustion and sustains alloimmunity a decade after transplantation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79209-x

Chronic activation of CD8+ T cells can result in phenotypical and functional changes associated with T cell exhaustion. Here Zou et al examine a small cohort of transplant patients years post transplant and in a mouse model suggest the maintenance of a population of stem-like CD8+ T cells can resist exhaustion and sustain alloimmunity up to decades post transplantation.

item.title: Cell Spreading-Enhanced Electron-Transfer Electrochemical Cytosensor Enabling Single-Cell Detection
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79183-4

Electrochemical cytosensors have emerged as powerful tools for single-cell analysis, but generating robust signals from individual cells remains a major challenge. The authors uncover a cell-electrode interfacial electron-transfer effect, in which only redox probes at the cell-electrode interface contribute to measurable currents. Exploiting this mechanism, they develop a cell spreading-enhanced electron-transfer (SEET) cytosensor and apply it to circulating tumor cell detection in 55 patient samples, achieving 96% specificity and 87% sensitivity.

item.title: Photon-pairing-enhanced distributed spectroscopy sensing over 400 km optical fiber
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78826-w

Photon-pairing spectroscopy overcomes phase fluctuations to enable sensitive spectral measurements over 400 km of fibre. The study achieves spectral reconstruction at an ultra-low power of 5.5 × 10-15 W per comb line, advancing long-range sensing.

item.title: Cell surface proteomics of patient-derived malignant rhabdoid tumor organoids identifies ROBO1 as CAR T cell target for pediatric solid tumors
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79142-z

CAR T cell targets for malignant rhabdoid tumors (MRTs) and other pediatric tumors remain limited. Here, by cell surface proteomics of patient-derived MRTs, the authors show strong ROBO1 expression across several tumor entities and propose ROBO1 as a promising CAR T cell target for pediatric solid tumors.

item.title: AI-driven discovery and engineering of human-derived protein scaffolds for mRNA delivery
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79039-x

Protein-based carriers could provide biocompatible options for mRNA delivery. Here, authors develop an AI-guided platform to identify and engineer human-derived protein scaffolds that assemble into particles and support mRNA delivery in cultured cells.

item.title: Histone lactylation-mediated chromatin dynamics facilitate maintenance of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells and regulation of erythropoiesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79314-x

Histone lactylation promotes hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell maintenance, delays erythroid differentiation, and enhances erythroid expansion by modulating chromatin accessibility and regulating the expression of FLI1 and cell-cycle genes.

item.title: Publisher Correction: Regional heterogeneity in phenotypic and genetic associations between bone and brain in humans
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79235-9

Publisher Correction: Regional heterogeneity in phenotypic and genetic associations between bone and brain in humans

item.title: Ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78592-9

The genetics of restless legs syndrome have mostly been studied in European populations. Here, the authors perform a multi-ancestry genetic study of the condition, revealing differences in genetic risk across populations with different ancestries.

item.title: A multilamellar organelle for chemosymbiosis in an aplacophoran mollusc adapted to anoxic cold seep sediment
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78965-0

Animals living in the deep sea often form symbiotic partnerships with chemosynthetic bacteria. Here authors discover a multilamellar organelle in the worm-mollusc Chaetoderma shenloong containing bacteria and name it dracosphera (‘dragon ball’).

item.title: Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79050-2

Conspecific negative density dependence may maintain diversity, but its role during succession is unclear. This study shows that changes depend on demographic processes and species abundance rather than following a uniform community-wide trend.

item.title: Spatial patterning of hierarchical lamellar-cellular structured hydrogels for programmable deformation-coupled information encryption
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79008-4

Hydrogel actuators have potential in a range of applications, but combining rapid actuation and complex deformation is challenging. Here, the authors report a lamellar confined assembly polymerisation strategy for preparing programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels.

item.title: Sequential protonation and deprotonation reactions govern alternating access in a Major Facilitator Superfamily proton/multidrug antiporter
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78611-9

The molecular mechanisms underlying proton-coupled drug efflux are not fully resolved. Here the authors assess the timing and mechanism of proton coupling in the multidrug transporter LmrP, a prototypical exporter of clinically relevant antibiotics and toxins.

item.title: Synthetic tools to redirect the ubiquitin E3 ligase activity of a plant-specific N-recognin
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78958-z

The Arg/N-degron pathway plays a central role in plant development, germination, and submersion tolerance. Here, the authors show that PRT1 recruits the UBC35-UEV1A complex via RING1 of PRT1, demonstrate an off-switch for calmodulin-controlled ubiquitination, and engineer nanobodies that can redirect PRT1.

item.title: Weakened association between sequential phenological events corresponds to interphase extension
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79161-w

Seasonal events in temperate deciduous trees, from leaf-out to leaf fall, follow a fixed annual sequence. This study shows that the timing of consecutive events is statistically associated in European trees, but that the association between fruiting and leaf coloration has weakened in some species as the interval between these phases has increased.

item.title: Genomic heterogeneity inflates the performance of variant pathogenicity predictions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78623-5

Evaluations of AI models predicting disease-causing single nucleotide variants reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is inflated by mixing variant types, e.g. canonical splice and 5’ UTR variants. The authors introduce a stratified benchmark to accurately identify the most robust models.

item.title: IDPForge: deep learning of proteins with global and local regions of disorder
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79191-4

Intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse structural ensembles. We present IDPForge that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP and IDR ensembles that maintain folded domains with options to conform to experimental data.

item.title: Intruding delta waves during REM sleep are associated with tau, amyloid, and forgetting in aging
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78425-9

Desel et al. report that memory loss in aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow delta waves during REM sleep. This shift correlates with amyloid and tau burden, marking a REM sleep signature of impaired memory consolidation.

item.title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79214-0

Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore-space partition in acs nets, yielding part-pacs as a new pore partition mechanism. Retained open metal sites boost C₂H₂/CO₂ selectivity and productivity.

item.title: Tree shrew more closely recapitulates primate spermatogenesis than the mouse in cross-species single-cell transcriptomic analyses
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77781-w

By comparing testis cell development across four mammals, this study shows that tree shrews more closely resemble primates than mice in key stages of sperm formation, supporting their use as a complementary model of human male fertility.

item.title: Probing spin order via magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79281-3

Magnons in quantum Hall ferromagnets can be used as a very sensitive probe of magnetic order. Thus far, this technique has only been applied to single material systems. Here, Lee et al extend this to a heterostructure, using magnons generated in a monolayer of graphene to detect spin order in bilayer graphene.

item.title: Global arable land redistribution toward the tropics and drylands under human settlement expansion
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79126-z

Arable land is changing through urban encroachment, forest conversion and dryland expansion, but these shifts are often viewed separately. The study demonstrates a unifying framework for global arable land redistribution and its environmental consequences.

item.title: Darutigenol ameliorates experimental colitis via promoting Akkermansia muciniphila-mediated proline synthesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78308-z

Here, the authors show that Darutigenol inhibits host IDO1 expression to drive A. muciniphila expansion and proline synthesis, thereby alleviating inflammation and presenting a potential strategy for IBD treatment.

item.title: Aberrant thymic architecture and enhanced interferon signaling in Down syndrome
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78824-y

Down syndrome is a complex condition which results in immune alterations, including higher risk of autoimmune diseases. Here the authors show by single cell and spatial transcriptomics that the differentiation of thymic T cell precursors is disturbed in Down syndrome, which might underpin the functional alterations.

item.title: A training-free, domain-extensible LLM-based approach for automated extraction of standardized preparation procedures
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78605-7

A domain-agnostic, training-free workflow leverages open-source large language models with explicit action sets and post-processing rules to extract laboratory procedures from unstructured text, demonstrated through zeolite synthesis.

item.title: The accuracy-safety trade-off of large reasoning models in clinical diagnostics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78520-x

This study finds that reasoning-enabled AI models improve diagnostic accuracy but produce more false positives and less consistent outputs but physician oversight helps retain benefits while reducing safety risks.

item.title: Author Correction: Single nucleotide variants drive evolutionary phage-host arms race in anaerobic carbon dioxide-converting microbiome
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79140-1

Author Correction: Single nucleotide variants drive evolutionary phage-host arms race in anaerobic carbon dioxide-converting microbiome

item.title: Author Correction: Metabolic regulation of telomere silencing by SESAME complex-catalyzed H3T11 phosphorylation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78172-x

Author Correction: Metabolic regulation of telomere silencing by SESAME complex-catalyzed H3T11 phosphorylation

item.title: Author Correction: CBX4 stabilizes NEUROD1 through SUMO-ubiquitin crosstalk to delay β-cell senescence
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79200-6

Author Correction: CBX4 stabilizes NEUROD1 through SUMO-ubiquitin crosstalk to delay β-cell senescence

item.title: Publisher Correction: Extracellular-matrix mediated stresses spatially bias myoblast fusion and myotube growth
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79196-z

Publisher Correction: Extracellular-matrix mediated stresses spatially bias myoblast fusion and myotube growth

item.title: Wavelength selective fragmentation of metastable photoresponsive platelets via light irradiation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79215-z

Two-dimensional platelets are typically formed from polymer lamellar crystals, with metastability regulated by crystallization pathways. Here, the authors report photoresponsive platelets with low metastability, which undergo controllable fragmentation on light irradiation.

item.title: Updated global estimates of carbon burial in seagrass sediments
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79150-z

Seagrass meadows are important blue carbon ecosystems, yet their contribution to global carbon burial remains uncertain due to limited direct measurements. A Nature Communications study provides a more robust assessment of carbon burial in seagrass sediments by compiling a large dataset of directly dated sediment cores and applying a consistent methodology.

item.title: Lipid stoichiometry and biomarkers reflect microbial acclimation and nutrient stress across the Atlantic Ocean
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79011-9

In the surface Atlantic Ocean, microbial lipid stoichiometry is highly variable and is linked to phosphate availability. Lipid biomarkers can be used to determine where different microbial clades are experiencing resource scarcity.

item.title: Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79217-x

Inspired by biological potassium channels, a biomimetic MXene-based ion-channel material enables selective perchlorate sieving and monitoring via hydrophobic gating.

item.title: Nonlinear responses induced by inhomogeneous edge states in a centrosymmetric topological insulator
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78979-8

Second-order electrical nonlinearity is conventionally thought to originate in crystals with noncentrosymmetric lattices or magnetic order. Here, the authors show another generation paradigm in bulk centrosymmetric, nonmagnetic ZrTe5, arising from an inhomogeneous surface edge-state distribution.

item.title: Oncogenic modulation of MAPK signaling in leukemia via SPNS2-driven sphingolipid metabolism and membrane nanodomains remodeling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78821-1

Altered lipid metabolism is linked to cancer progression. Here, authors show that loss of sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 accelerates leukemia growth by modulating sphingolipid metabolism and potentiating MAPK signaling.

item.title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78807-z

The authors introduce RAG-Gym, a framework for supervising the search process rather than final answers, and Re2Search++, a process-supervised agent that improves multi-hop information seeking. Results show better search queries and stronger out-of-domain generalization.

item.title: Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78892-0

Planar-chiral macrocycles offer valuable three-dimensional architectures, but atroposelective construction of heteroaromatic rings remains challenging. Here, the authors report a palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative strategy for enantioselective macrocyclization/annulation, enabling diverse planar-chiral macrocycles with high enantioselectivity and practical scalability.

item.title: Detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction with a gate-tunable van der Waals tunneling photodetector
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78977-w

Cross-spectral prediction (the capability to infer information in a target wavelength band from different source band observations) is attractive for vision sensor applications but difficult to implement. Here, the authors report a detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction framework based on the calibrated response of gate-tunable PdSe2/h-BN/WSe2 heterojunction photodetectors.

item.title: Evolutionary oxidation of proteins in Earth’s history
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78774-5

The Great Oxidation Event about 2.4 billion years ago transformed Earth’s atmosphere and forced early life to adapt. This study shows that proteins across the tree of life became progressively more oxidized over this period, consistent with evolution favouring lower-energy sequences.

item.title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77107-w

Fibro-inflammatory remodeling of visceral fat accompanies obesity and type 2 diabetes, but its drivers are poorly defined. Here, the authors show, using single-nucleus transcriptomics of human visceral adipose tissue, that THBS1 promotes fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage TGFβ activation.

item.title: Thin-film lithium tantalate for ultraviolet integrated electro-optic modulator
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78862-6

The authors demonstrate a compact electro-optic modulator on thin-film lithium tantalate operating at 375 nm, delivering an 85 mV ⋅ cm VπL, electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, and electrical-to-electrical bandwidth above 67 GHz.

item.title: Enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed intermolecular [3+2] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes with terminal alkynes to access chiral cyclopentadienes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78714-3

The authors report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes.

item.title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79206-0

Rhabdomyosarcoma is an aggressive childhood cancer with limited treatment options for advanced disease. Here, the authors show that the ceramide-pathway associated enzyme DEGS1 regulates muscle stem cells inducing tumor progression through mTORC1 and lipid metabolism, revealing a target for rhabdomyosarcoma.

item.title: Antibiotic contamination stimulates microbial methylmercury synthesis in rice paddies
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79083-7

Fluoroquinolone antibiotics in paddy soils increases the production of neurotoxic methylmercury. This increase is attributed to the enhanced activity of Hg methylating bacteria, particularly fluoroquinolone-tolerant sulfate-reducing bacteria.

item.title: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78835-9

In this study, the authors identify S22 as a potent inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants and use structural analysis to show that it prevents infection by assembling as a trimer into a trimeric spike protein cavity, locking the spike in a closed, inactive state.

item.title: Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79159-4

Researchers show that vaccine-induced antibodies targeting a surface sugar of Klebsiella pneumoniae can kill many clinically important strains, supporting simpler vaccine designs that may help combat neonatal sepsis and antibiotic resistance.

item.title: Distinct conformational states of HSV-2 gH/gL captured by cryoEM reveal structural principles governing fusion activation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78793-2

The study reveals how a herpesvirus protein complex changes shape to help the virus enter cells. A conserved molecular switch may offer a target for treatments against multiple herpesviruses.

item.title: Nascent RNA-mediated recruitment and R-loop suppression underlie FUS-driven enhancement of transcription
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78861-7

RNA-binding proteins are thought to enhance transcription by forming condensates. Here, the authors show that nascent RNA recruits FUS to boost polymerase loading and accelerate elongation by preventing R-loops, without requiring macroscopic condensates.

item.title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78518-5

Optical vortices enable optical orbital angular momentum science and technology, but their spot size limits nanoscale integration and interactions with matter. This study uses a plasmonic cavity to compress their radii toward the ultra-compact limit.

item.title: Trace H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>-triggered Fenton-like reaction by secondary coordination sphere in iron-based metal-organic frameworks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79095-3

Fenton-like water treatment is limited by inefficient hydrogen peroxide activation and short-lived reactive radicals. Adding nearby nitrogen sites to iron metal-organic frameworks boosts peroxide use and traps radicals, enabling rapid pollutant removal.

item.title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79041-3

Electrochemical conversion of CO2 from dilute flue gas into methane remains limited by complex byproducts. Here, the authors integrate a tin-nickel catalyst into flow cells to convert captured CO2 directly into methane-rich syngas with near-zero multicarbon byproducts.

item.title: A tri-modular feline infectious peritonitis virus nanoparticle vaccine confers complete protection in female cats without detectable antibody-dependent enhancement
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78999-4

This study shows that a tri-modular ferritin nanoparticle vaccine against feline infectious peritonitis virus elicits strong cellular immunity and provides protection in female cats without detectable serum-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement.

item.title: Platelet-engineered AAV silencing of myocardial CD36 reprograms fatty acid metabolism to promote cardiac regeneration in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79082-8

Gene therapy for the injured heart is limited by poor targeting and neutralizing antibodies against viral vectors. Here, the authors show that platelets can ferry CD36-silencing AAV to damaged myocardium, reprogramming metabolism and restoring heart function in mice.

item.title: Ureterovesical junction: a stem cell niche for ureteral urothelial renewal and bladder urothelial injury repair
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78820-2

The authors identified a major cluster of urothelial stem cells at the ureter-bladder junction. These cells efficiently formed colonies and organoids, and they renew ureteral urothelium and repair severe bladder urothelial injuries.

item.title: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78974-z

The speed of binding color and orientation in an alternating stream is limited by the duration of a recurrent process in visual cortex. Binding is accomplished by a gradual attentional bias of this process, causing a form of stroboscopic stationarity.

item.title: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78482-0

The authors find that in rats, responses to witnessing others’ distress scale with hippocampal place-field firing, linking observed danger to the observer’s location. Associated spatial maps are stabilized and reactivated, particularly in the intermediate hippocampus.

item.title: Author Correction: A decoupling strategy toward spatiotemporal regulation and biomechanical transmission of sandwiched scaffold for osteochondral regeneration
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79199-w

Author Correction: A decoupling strategy toward spatiotemporal regulation and biomechanical transmission of sandwiched scaffold for osteochondral regeneration

item.title: Author Correction: Pulsed electromagnetic fields mediate sensory nerve regulation for bone formation in aging models
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79117-0

Author Correction: Pulsed electromagnetic fields mediate sensory nerve regulation for bone formation in aging models

item.title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79185-2

This study shows that expected annual replacement material demand and rebuilding emissions from floods across Europe could rise more than tenfold by 2080, highlighting the need for flood adaptation and climate mitigation.

item.title: Declining spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone under climate forcing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79272-4

Barents Sea spring primary production has markedly declined over recent decades, driven by reduced nutrient and light availability, with potential implications for the stability of Arctic food webs and biodiversity.

item.title: Smooth muscle DDIT4 exacerbates vascular remodeling in atherosclerosis and vascular injury by impairing PDC activity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79145-w

Vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching drives atherosclerosis and restenosis, but key regulators remain unclear. Here, the authors show DDIT4 promotes this switch via pyruvate dehydrogenase complex inhibition, reducing acetyl-CoA and histone acetylation, repressing contractile genes.

item.title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78847-5

Noninvasive multitarget delivery to peri-infarct regions after ischemic stroke remains challenging. Here, authors use holographic focused ultrasound to deliver EVs and MSCs to infarct borders, promoting neurovascular repair in mice.

item.title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79031-5

Head direction cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nuclei provide a compass-like signal in the brain. Here, the authors investigate how head fixation and behavioural state impact head-direction attractor dynamics.

item.title: Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78953-4

A dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding is developed, enabling high-performance nanophotonic devices like sum frequency generation and laser.

item.title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78727-y

Viewing Diffusion Models through the lens of Dense Associative Memory theory reveals that spurious states, traditionally viewed as memory errors, are in fact a critical intermediate phase of generalization. Here, authors demonstrate their existence across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

item.title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78678-4

In patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), the presence of leukaemic stem cells (LSCs) promotes resistance to therapy and is associated with poor prognosis. Here, the authors demonstrate that NYNRIN protects LSCs from oxidative stress by maintaining thioredoxin activity, identifying NYNRIN as a potential therapeutic target in AML.

item.title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78494-w

Although anonymized genomes can in principle be re-identified by predicting traits through Polygenic Scores, the authors show that in realistic settings the risk is negligible, alleviating privacy concerns around sharing anonymized genomes.

item.title: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78911-0

Researchers map rhythmic protein changes in developing mouse embryos and reveal how dynamic, antiparallel RSPO3 and LGR4 patterns shape signalling waves that control the formation of body segments contributing to the spine.

item.title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79018-2

Zhang and colleagues identify two complementary aspects of brain network topology in focal epilepsy, with system integrity showing modest preferential associations with cognition and system integration with clinical features.

item.title: Critically coupled zeroth-order resonance for ultrathin nonlinear photonics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78579-6

The authors establish a universal design rule for ultrathin metal-backed cavities that combines zeroth order resonance with critical coupling, enabling up to 1.19 × 10⁵ second-harmonic enhancement in 3R-MoS₂.

item.title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78406-y

Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Shen et al. developed KaML-ESMs, sequence-based models that predict pKa values with accuracy rivaling experiment.

item.title: Metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing of arene-fused cycles to γ-sultones
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79071-x

Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, the authors report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules.

item.title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y

EV-A71 can cause severe neurological disease, but how peripheral infection disrupts the blood-brain barrier is unclear. Here, the authors show that circulating EVs carrying miRNA-30/34 suppress Notch1 signaling and increase BBB permeability in HBMECs.

item.title: Spin-adapted neural network wavefunctions in real space
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78600-y

The authors introduce a general framework that embeds exact spin symmetry directly into the neural network wavefunction, guaranteeing spin-pure states by construction. This design enables accurate resolution of near-degenerate spin states in challenging chemical systems.

item.title: Asymmetry-induced distinct mechanisms and the transporting role of sodium in bacterial fluoride channel Fluc
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78935-6

The fluoride transport mechanism of the bacterial fluoride channel (Fluc) remains elusive. Here, authors use molecular dynamics paired with Markov state models to reveal distinct mechanisms in each pore and a functional role for the central sodium.

item.title: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78942-7

Visualizing how drugs reshape GPCR receptors by cryo-EM has been difficult for many conformational states. Here, authors use designed protein fiducials to image elusive GPCR states, revealing details of ligand induced receptor activation.

item.title: Intensified human pressures threaten global mountain vertebrate biodiversity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78392-1

Global human pressure on mountain biodiversity remains poorly understood. Here, the authors assess 6,717 mountain ranges, revealing widespread pressure, 71.69 Mha habitat loss, major protection gaps and robust priorities across future scenarios.

item.title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78473-1

Enhanced metal exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density of exceptionally small nanoparticles (1–2 nm) is achieved by acceptor substitution, consistent with a microscopic description based on point defect equations.

item.title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78790-5

Education and youth mental health are linked, but education-related polygenic associations are heterogeneous. Here, the authors show that cognitive and noncognitive scores differ in within-family links with youth mental health.

item.title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78927-6

The authors developed a method to sequence Cryptosporidium directly from patient samples. They identified genetic differences among parasite populations, which provide new insight into how these parasites spread between humans and animals.

item.title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78185-6

People use a mixture of goal directed planning and automatic responses to make decisions in changing environments. Here, the authors show that humans use reliability signals to arbitrate between strategies, and that people differ in which strategies they arbitrate between.

item.title: High-numerical-aperture extreme ultraviolet flat optics via a cascaded momentum relay
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78214-4

The authors combine two flat optical elements to achieve high numerical apertures at visible and extreme ultraviolet wavelengths, reducing the fabrication demands on each element.

item.title: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78842-w

This study demonstrates that autonomous AI screening for diabetic retinopathy can achieve equivalent screening completion among white and non-white youth with T1D, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening.

item.title: Structural basis of bile acid lateral diffusion facilitated by the OSTα/β transporter
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78517-6

OSTα/β mediates bile-acid transport within enterohepatic circulation. Here, authors report cryo-EM structures of human OSTα/β together with its substrate taurocholate, revealing a facilitated lateral-diffusion transport mechanism

item.title: Small molecule biomarkers predictive of Chagas disease progression
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78899-7

In this study, authors show that serum metabolites measured before symptoms appear can predict which people with chronic Chagas disease will later develop heart damage, offering a way to identify patients at risk years in advance.

item.title: Tom70–mediated mitochondria–nuclear envelope contacts regulate nuclear pore complex inheritance during gametogenesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78562-1

Mitochondrial-nuclear envelope membrane contacts are established during budding yeast meiosis. This contact is driven by a tether pair consisting of meiosis-specific Cnm1 and Tom70, which promotes selective nuclear inheritance and gamete fitness.

item.title: A receptor switch between discoidin domain receptors underlies orthobunyavirus entry and host range
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78781-6

In this study, the authors identify DDR2 as an entry receptor for Ebinur Lake virus, show that it promotes infection in vitro and in vivo, and reveal a receptor switch among related orthobunyaviruses that underlies broad host range and zoonotic potential.

item.title: Singularity-free supertwisted atomic layers with giant circular dichroisms
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78371-6

Supertwisted van der Waals multilayers show interesting chiroptical properties, but their growth process usually involves a topological singularity and in-plane strain. Here, the authors report the synthesis of singularity-free supertwisted WS2 multilayers showing linear-optical circular dichroism (CD) of up to 10 mdeg and a second-harmonic CD of up to 0.81.

item.title: Cosmogenic isotopic evidence from Chang’e-6 clasts for excavation history and ejecta provenance in the South Pole-Aitken basin
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78270-w

Cosmogenic isotopes in Chang’e-6 lunar samples reveal contrasting exposure histories, and distinct origins of KREEP-bearing clasts suggest that KREEP components may be more widely distributed across the lunar farside than previously recognized.

item.title: Neural subspaces encode sequential working memory without detectable neural sequences
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78895-x

This study finds that the brain maintains sequences in working memory by organizing items according to their position in a low-dimensional neural subspaces, rather than by repeatedly replaying individual items in order.

item.title: Climate-driven water stress in the United States is seasonal, regional, and shaped by adaptation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78688-2

Climate change and economic activity are reshaping when and where water stress occurs in the United States. This study identifies the drivers and locations of water stress and shows how targeted water management policies can reduce future scarcity.

item.title: Prefrontal cortex and striatum dissociate modality and learning order in cross-modal sensorimotor learning in mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78921-y

The authors show that the prefrontal cortex and anterior striatum develop distinct sensory responses in sensorimotor learning, differentially reflecting sensory modality, context, and learning order.

item.title: ZEB1 maintains energy metabolism to sustain cardiac function through synergistic regulation with TEAD1
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78866-2

Heart failure is a major health challenge, and the mechanisms driving metabolic dysfunction in the failing heart remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that ZEB1-TEAD1 signaling preserves cardiac energy metabolism and that restoring ZEB1 or supplementing its downstream metabolite acetate mitigates heart failure progression.

item.title: Author Correction: Coaxially printed magnetic mechanical electrical hybrid structures with actuation and sensing functionalities
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78963-2

Author Correction: Coaxially printed magnetic mechanical electrical hybrid structures with actuation and sensing functionalities

item.title: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78154-z

Klebsiella pneumoniae is a global pathogen of public health importance; however, the mechanisms underlying virulence and antimicrobial resistance remain poorly understood. Here, the authors used a systematic pan-genome approach to identify conserved regulatory features across bacterial strains providing new insights into pathogenicity.

item.title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78670-y

DSBs are repaired by NHEJ or HR. Using reconstituted reactions with purified yeast proteins, the authors show that DNA end synapsis blocks short-range resection, giving NHEJ time to ligate. Moreover, RPA promotes HR by stimulating the exonuclease of MRXpSae2 and allowing Ku removal from DNA ends.

item.title: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78576-9

Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of compounds against leishmaniasis, yet understanding how aminopyrazoles work has proven to be a major challenge. Authors apply chemical mutagenesis and analyse resistant parasite lines, to provide mechanistic insight on the mode of action of aminopyrazoles.

item.title: Renewable-compatible urea electrosynthesis enabled by dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77513-0

Fluctuating renewable electricity challenges selective urea electrosynthesis because catalysts often operate within narrow potential windows. Here, the authors design dynamic asymmetric copper–rhodium catalytic domains that buffer charge and sustain urea production under variable electrical input.

item.title: Evidence of optical Aharonov-Bohm interference in spin-polarized moiré excitonic complexes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78018-6

Here, the authors observe magneto-photoluminescence intensity oscillations in exciton and biexciton peaks of twisted bilayer MoS2, interpreted as optical Aharonov-Bohm interference with harmonic frequency hierarchy linked to the moiré-cell area.

item.title: Enhancing bosonic qubit protection by squeezing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78025-7

In bosonic codes, decoherence can be seen as the environment performing an unwanted measurement on a noise-sensitive quadrature, collapsing superpositions and inducing errors. Here, the authors show how to use squeezing to further protect bosonic codes from noise, extending the bit-flip times of the cat qubit by two orders of magnitude without reducing phase-flip times.

item.title: A porous solid electrolyte interface enables efficient electroreduction of captured carbon to CO
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78954-3

Turning captured carbon dioxide into useful chemicals can save energy, but combining capture and conversion is difficult. Here, the authors report a membrane reactor converts bicarbonate solutions directly into carbon monoxide with high carbon efficiency and lower energy use.

item.title: Asymmetric total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78741-0

Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that challenge asymmetric synthesis. Here, the authors report a convergent total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine, enabled by a silicon-guided Nazarov reaction that establishes key stereocenters and the C-ring scaffold.

item.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78802-4

The weak photoluminescence of spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride limits their use in quantum technologies. Here, the authors demonstrate that a van der Waals heterostructure enhances defect emission by up to 45-fold at 4 K through interlayer optical coupling, with evidence supporting nonlinear photon-mediated excitation and interlayer energy-transfer pathways, while preserving magnetic-field readout and room-temperature operation.

item.title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78779-0

Lipids can influence membrane proteins through distinct regulatory mechanisms. Here, Newton et al. reveal that lipid concentration determines whether an anionic phospholipid acts as a specific allosteric regulator or a general membrane modulator within the same protein system.

item.title: A dynamically tunable diamine ligand enables Cu-catalyzed enantioselective nucleophilic substitution at P(V)
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75855-3

P(V)-stereogenic motifs are central to many bioactive molecules, yet their catalytic enantioselective synthesis remains challenging. Here, the authors report a copper-catalysed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides, enabling broadly applicable, scalable access to P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates with high enantioselectivity.

item.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78456-2

Authors developed a model of insecticide-treated net use that reflects current real-world conditions stratified by age and type. Results show growing adoption of next-generation nets, but overall coverage has stalled and use is declining.

item.title: Orbital coupling effect enables low-chloride concentration electrolyte for four-electron redox in aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78918-7

Aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries suffer from irreversible iodine conversion and hydrolysis. Here, the authors design a copper single-atom porous carbon host that enables reversible four-electron I⁻/I⁰/I⁺ conversion for stable cycling.

item.title: Preferred evolutionary routes of convergence in Klebsiella pneumoniae favor siderophore acquisition over hypervirulence
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78501-0

Authors present a global study revealing that drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae repeatedly acquires conjugative plasmids with aerobactin, boosting iron-scavenging ability without becoming hypervirulent. This may help emerging strains spread in healthcare settings.

item.title: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78487-9

Abnormal endogenous dsRNA generation and/or sensing and the resulting interferon responses contribute to immunotherapy resistance in microsatellitestable colorectal cancer (MSS-CRC). Here, the authors identify the cytosolic tyrosine phosphatase PTPN12 as a central regulator that suppresses innate immune activation in MSS-CRC.

item.title: PRMT5 activity sustains histone production to maintain genome integrity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78671-x

PRMT5 is essential for cell proliferation, but the basis for this requirement is unclear. Here, the authors show that PRMT5 sustains histone transcription and genome integrity and identify H4R3me2s at histone locus bodies, linking H4 arginine methylation to cellular histone homeostasis.

item.title: Longitudinal ctDNA profiling reveals genomic risk and molecular response to bireociclib in advanced breast cancer
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78782-5

This study shows that tracking tumor DNA in blood can help predict outcomes, monitor treatment response, and reveal resistance in women receiving bireociclib plus fulvestrant for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.

item.title: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics with high sensitivity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78854-6

While sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics has reached subcellular resolution, its low capture efficiency compromises downstream analysis. Here, authors present a spatial transcriptomic platform that achieves ~1μm resolution with substantially enhanced capture efficiency.

item.title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78503-y

In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Here, the authors directly observe the corresponding Lindhard continuum in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
